item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I don't think they did, once his younger self went through. But they had to let the events that lead to the current timeline play out first or risk a temporal paradox. I suspect Ambridge will be having an unpleasant time of it from now on but he's accepted that, having had a long fulfilling life he otherwise wouldn't have.

I like the standardized containment procedures and wish more writers would put some of those.
But I'm not sure they'd leave the researcher unpunished. Or still employed.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Thank you for taking the time to comment! It's really encouraging and helpful when people say what they think. I'm glad you liked it! I did actually have a test log in my first draft, but I edited it out when I pared the article down: it didn't really add much to the tale. You can safely assume that the tests included things like mice and goats and human test subjects, and the results gave them their return time estimates.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I really enjoyed this rewrite. It added an emotional level most SCPs can't touch on. It's a tale wrapped up inside a report. My only issue is the lack of any test logs or listings, even though they are referenced early in the article. I'm curious as to what else was put through (esp. 5-12) before our researcher broke the system?

Otherwise awesome. +1

I understand why the foundation doesn't want to send anyone anymore in, but it looks too short.

Such a vast improvement on the original. Sometimes less is more; it certainly was here.
This one gives me a serious case of the feels.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I understand your misgivings. The time-travel is an addition of mine to the original SCP, to add some interest and story to it.

The short answer is: they don't know for sure. But they do know that one D-class that went in ended up in the past, breaching containment. So that's a pretty good incentive not to risk sending any more in. In my mind, containment > research.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: It's an interesting story, I'll give you that, but I just can't shake the idea that it goes completely against what the description says this anomaly does. I mean, it could be the exception proving the rule, or just that the Foundation doesn't actually know everything about it, but it's bothering me for some reason. Plus, how do they know the things that come out of it really are the same as what goes in?

item.title: (no title)

item.title: 664 rewrite.
item.content:encoded:
Original writer: Dr. Cooper - April 28, 2009 - "The Floor to Nowhere"

Thank you to Doctor Anborough and others for allowing me this opportunity to revive an old classic. This is one of the first SCPs I remember reading when I first learned of this site some years ago, and it is an honour to have the chance to keep it alive. I hope you all enjoy the changes I have made. Doctor Anborough will, I believe, be adding in the old screen-caps for the article and the discussion pages.
